title: 2100 beats 2200
transcript: Fools will get checkmated, but I was no fool in this game. This was my highest rated win ever in an online game. When the game happened, my opponent was rated 2205, and I was sitting at my peak rating, 2117. A rating disparity of almost 100 points. My opponent here attacked my rook, and I saw the opportunity to bring it up with rook to F3. Now, building up pressure around the black king, but my opponent's idea was to play knight to F5, now blocking the view of the bishop and trying to remove some of my pieces. But, as you might know, I've been preparing to play the Grand Prix Festival, and I've been studying a lot of chess. So, I knew that I was completely winning, and I just had to find how. The idea of bringing the rook to G3 was too appealing. So, I gave a bishop over that knight, and then played rook to G3. Now, I am threatening to win this pawn on the next move, because the other black pawn is pinned to the black king. And, of course, if my opponent pushes, I'm going to win this pawn, and then bring the bishop threatening a checkmate. So, my opponent played bishop takes D5, now removing the knight and defending the square at the same time. Now, here, believe it or not, I can ignore the bishop and still take here, because the bishop is going to hang on the next move. And, if you try to save it, I'm going to take like this. But, it was not 100% clear to me what happens after G6. So, instead, I decided to take the bishop and maintain this attack, because I saw that after the king moves, which is what happened in the game, I had a brilliant attack starting with the beautiful bishop F6, sacrificing my bishop completely to create a checkmate threat in two moves. If black plays a random move, I'm going to take here, and on the next move give a checkmate like this. But, the bishop cannot be taken. If you take here, I am now going to bring the rook to H3 and prepare another checkmate. There is no way to defend this pawn. The queen is too far away. These black pawns work as a wall for their own queen. And, if you try to create an escape route for your king like this, of Of we're not going to take like this. instead we have queen takes F7 with another checkmate. So, my opponent played G6, now attacking the queen and forcing it to move. And here I was considering to just retreat and build a battery with the rook on the next move, but that is a little bit slow and unnecessary because I have another brilliant move with queen takes H6, a beautiful little sacrifice but with a pretty simple idea. Of course, if you don't take this is going to be a checkmate on the next move, but if you take this is going to be another checkmate. And just like that I got my peak rating of 2127 beating a 2200 rated player. I'll keep studying and practicing and hopefully have a great performance at the Grand Chess Festival.
